_comment: THE PRODUCER SEAM'S MEMBER CENSUS AND ITS RULE TABLE. Data-Contract.md §5.
THIS FILE IS DATA FOR THE REASON `refusal-reasons.json` AND `snapshot-format.json` ARE:
two languages need it. `src/blocktracer/chain/contract_rules.nim` reads it with
`staticRead` at compile time — so a malformed table fails the BUILD — and
`tools/chain/snapshot-contract-selftest.mjs` reads it to check the reader against it.
It is §5's member census in machine-readable form: for every container the reader
opens, every member it consumes, whether the CONTRACT requires that member, and which
SUBSCRIPT the reader reaches it with. The two are different facts and conflating them
is what this whole deliverable exists to end:
required   what §5 says a producer must write
access     what `ingest.nim` does — `node["k"]` raises on absence, `node{"k"}` does not
A member that is OPTIONAL to the contract and reached by `[]` is a member the reader
crashes on and the spec says is fine. That is not a hypothetical: `provenance.l1ChainId`
was exactly that, §5.2 named none of the four provenance members the summary writer
reached, and the live follower's own mainnet output omitted it — so the producer this
repository ships wrote a snapshot the reader this repository ships raised `KeyError` on,
invisibly, because every committed fixture carried the member.
A member that is REQUIRED by the contract and reached by `{}` is legitimate exactly when
some rule enforces it by name instead; `enforcedBy` names that rule, and the checker
requires one. `format` is the archetype: read with `{}` so an absent token does not
raise inside `std/json`, then refused by name against the readable set.
A member §5 names that this reader does not consume must say who does. Without it the
census would quietly accumulate members nothing reads, which is the other direction of
the same defect and the direction `counts` sat in: §5.2 required it, the reader never
opened it, and the tally's whole stated purpose — 'so a partial ingest is detectable' —
was served by nobody.
── WHY `defaultPath` IS HERE AND NOT IN THE READER ───────────────────────────────────
§5.1's rule is that every path but `snapshot.json` is named by the row that owns it.
FIVE of them carry a default for a capture whose row is silent — the four per-row
sidecars and the one snapshot-wide one — and a row's `container` carries none, because
it is required of every traced row and a row that names none is refused. A default
open-coded in the reader is a convention; a default stated in the contract is part of
the contract. So the reader spells none of the five and takes all five from here, and
`snapshot-contract-selftest.mjs` §8 fails if any of them appears as a path literal in
the reader — which it did, for `sources`, until 2026-09-17.

S5-SNAPSHOT-PRESENT.statement: A snapshot is a directory holding `snapshot.json`; that one file is read by name.

S5-FORMAT-UNKNOWN.statement: A `format` token the reader does not support is refused by name, naming the tokens the build accepts, and nothing is read.

S5-CHAIN-NAMED.statement: `provenance.chain` is required and is never guessed.

S5-CHAIN-UNIQUE.statement: A chain slug another producer already owns is refused at ingest rather than resolved.

S5-MEMBERS-REQUIRED.statement: Every member §5.2's table marks required is present; a snapshot short of one is refused naming the member rather than raising where it is first reached.

S5-ROW-MEMBERS-REQUIRED.statement: Every member §5.2b marks required and reaches by an unguarded subscript is present on the row that must carry it; a row short of one is refused naming the row and the member rather than raising inside the JSON reader.

S5-COUNTS-PRESENT.statement: `counts` is required: a snapshot with no tally has no detector for a partial ingest.

S5-COUNTS-ROWS.statement: `counts.blocks` and `counts.transactions` are measurements of the rows beside them and must equal their lengths.

S5-COUNTS-RECONCILE.statement: On `@2`, `counts.accountedFor` ranges over traced, untraced and chain-absent and equals `counts.transactions`.

S5-BLOCKS-ORDER.statement: `blocks` is newest first: every entry's height is at most its predecessor's. §5.2 has stated the order since it was written and nothing enforced it, so a producer that enumerated oldest-first published a tree whose order was the opposite of the one the contract promised.

S5-RECORDER-LABEL-UNIQUE.statement: Two recorder commits in one snapshot that shorten to one version label are refused; the label is what the build hash is derived from.

S5-CONTAINER-NONEMPTY.statement: A row that names a container must name one with bytes in it.

S5-CONTAINER-BYTES.statement: `containerBytes` is a measurement of the container the row names and must equal its size on disk; it is republished on the overlay row, so a figure that does not is a published number about a file nobody measured.

S5-REASON-REQUIRED.statement: A row that carries no trace carries a `reason`, and an empty reason is refused rather than published.

S5-REFUSALREASON-REQUIRED.statement: On `@2` every untraced row carries a `refusalReason`; a row without one is refused, naming the row.

S5-REFUSALREASON-CLOSED.statement: `refusalReason` is drawn from a closed set; a value outside it is refused rather than carried or dropped.

S5-REFUSALREASON-FORBIDDEN.statement: A chain-absent row carries the sentence and NOT the member; the closed set is a set of things this pipeline did.

S5-OUTCOME-CLOSED.statement: `transactions[].outcome` is drawn from a closed set, verbatim; a value outside it is refused naming the whole set, because §5.2's three populations are disjoint BY CONSTRUCTION only if every outcome belongs to one of them — an unrecognised token is a fourth, unpoliced bucket in which the rules that range over the populations silently do not fire.

S5-BUNDLE-REQUIRED.statement: A recording that claims source level, or one whose positions were computed post-hoc, is refused without a source bundle beside it. A recording that merely CARRIES a position stream is not: it is refused only when a bundle file is present beside it and holds no bundle. This statement said "or that carries positions" until 2026-09-17 and that disjunct was one the reader never enforced — the shipped template's own second row carries a position stream and no bundle, and conforms.

S5-BUNDLE-KEYED.statement: A source bundle is keyed by contract-class identity; one with no `codeHash` cannot be reached from a manifest.

S5-BUNDLE-NONEMPTY.statement: A source bundle with no files is refused rather than published and then recommended.

S5-INSTRUCTIONS-AGREE.statement: An instruction listing whose step count differs from the recording's is refused at publish time.

S5-POSITIONS-AGREE.statement: A position stream whose step count differs from the recording's is refused at publish time.

S5-POSITIONS-COLUMNS.statement: Every column of a position stream is as long as the recording's step count; a partial column would mark rows it was never measured for.

S5-CALLTRACE-AGREE.statement: A call trace's frame count must be the recording's `callsOpened` plus the synthetic top-level frame.

S5-CALLTRACE-FRAMES.statement: A call trace must carry as many frames as it declares.

S5-CALLTRACE-FOLD-NONEMPTY.statement: A frame marked folded claims something is behind it; folding with zero hidden descendants is refused.

S5-CALLTRACE-FOLD-TALLY.statement: A call trace's fold summary must be the sum its own frames carry.

S5-CALLTRACE-FOLD-BOUND.statement: A call trace may not fold more steps than the recording has.

S5-SIDECAR-FORMAT-UNKNOWN.statement: A sidecar that carries its own version token is refused by name when that token is one the reader does not support.

S5-SIDECAR-CHAIN.statement: A sidecar that names a chain must name this snapshot's; attaching one chain's answers to another's transactions is refused.

S5-RECORDER-STATED.statement: `provenance.recorder` states the recorder's id and the trace schema it writes; a snapshot that states neither is refused, because a recorder identity supplied by the reader is the reader deciding which chain produced the capture.

S5-PRESTATE-STATED.statement: `provenance.prestateStrategy` states how the producer obtained the state each execution ran against; a snapshot that does not is refused.

S5-PRESTATE-CLOSED.statement: `provenance.prestateStrategy` is drawn from a closed set, verbatim; a value outside it is refused naming the set, because a producer emitting an unlisted strategy is a gap in the table rather than a producer using a free-text field.

S5-COST-VECTOR.statement: A row's cost is a VECTOR the producer states, and every entry names itself and carries a figure; the reader supplies no name, unit or token, because a cost the reader named is a page that looks right and states the wrong cost. The vector carries at least one entry: a rule that ranges over entries is vacuously clean on zero of them, and an empty vector publishes a transaction page with no cost at all — indistinguishable from a producer that forgot, in the one seam this contract supplies no default for.

S5-EXECUTIONS-NAMED.statement: A row names the executions it holds, each by its own selector; the reader supplies none, because a selector the reader supplied collapses a chain's execution partition into a single unnamed one.

S5-EXECUTIONS-ONE-TRACED.statement: At most one of a row's executions may be left without its own reason — the one the row's container belongs to — and a traced row must leave exactly one, because a row carries one container and two executions claiming it would publish one recording as evidence of two.

S5-POSITIONS-SCHEMA.statement: A position stream states its own schema token, which is republished verbatim; a stream that states none is refused rather than published under a token the reader chose for it.

_prestateStrategiesComment: THE CLOSED SET `provenance.prestateStrategy` IS DRAWN FROM.
It is the six rows of Chain-Support-Matrix.md §1.4, verbatim, and it is DATA here for the
reason the refusal-reason set and the rule table are: two languages need it, the reader
refuses a value outside it by name, and a set spelled twice is two sets.
§1.4 states the rule this list implements: a producer emitting a value that is not in the
table is A GAP IN THAT SECTION, not a producer exercising a free-text field, and the
remedy is a row there — never a new string in a snapshot. So a term added here without a
row there is the failure this file cannot see; what it can hold is that the reader draws
from a stated set rather than from whatever a snapshot says.
_chainVocabularyComment: THE VOCABULARY THE READER MAY NOT SPELL. Data-Contract.md §5.3.
§5.3's whole subject is that the reader is chain-PARAMETERISED in every dimension that
reaches a URL and was chain-CONSTANT in six that do not. Once those six are read out of
the snapshot, the property worth holding is not 'those six literals are gone' — it is
that NO SEVENTH arrives. A literal naming a chain, a VM, a fee token or an ecosystem
language is how one arrives, every time, and it arrives looking like a small convenience.
`chainVocabularyLiterals` in `lib/reader-contract.mjs` matches each term below,
case-insensitively, against the reader's CODE — prose comments and doc comments
stripped, and `&`-joined string literals SPLICED first so `"azt" & "ec"` reads as one
token. The splice does NOT require the quotes to touch the operator (`("azt") & ("ec")`
is the same evasion), and it resolves a `&`-adjacent name bound to a single literal
(`"azt" & suffixEc`) before joining. It matches an identifier as readily as a string,
because a `const aztecFee` names a chain exactly as loudly as `"aztec"` does.
The boundary is not `\b` and not a plain non-alphanumeric run: a match is admitted at a
non-alphanumeric boundary OR at an uppercase letter following a lowercase one or a digit
— so `aztecFee`, `feeInGas` and `gasUsed` all match — and is rejected when a LOWERCASE
letter follows it, which is what keeps `manage` off `mana` and `gasoline` off `gas`.
── WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED ────────────────────────────────
* A PROSE COMMENT. Deliberate, and it is the reason the scan strips them: the reader's
comments record which chain a decision was measured on and why, and a comment cannot
reach a published object. The count of comment occurrences is REPORTED by the check
rather than written down here, so the figure cannot go stale.
* A NAME SYNTHESISED AT RUNTIME OR AT COMPILE TIME from characters — `chr(97) & …`, a
`staticRead` of a file this list does not cover, a `strformat` assembly. No text scan
can see those, and pretending otherwise is worse than saying so.
* A TERM FOLLOWED BY A LOWERCASE LETTER — `"aztecnet"`, `"myaztecchain"`. This is the
OTHER HALF of the boundary rule above rather than an oversight: the clause that lets
a correct reader write `manage` and `gasoline` is the same clause that lets those
through, and there is no version of the rule that has one without the other.
* A NAME ACCUMULATED RATHER THAN JOINED — `var s = "azt"` then `s.add "ec"`. The splice
reads one expression; an accumulation spreads the operands over statements.
* A VALUE THE READER OBTAINS FROM DATA. That is not an evasion, it is the point: the
snapshot, `identifier-encodings.json`, `refusal-reasons.json` and this file are where
such values belong, and a reader reading one of them names no chain.
Each of the four is PLANTED and asserted to be MISSED by §9 of the selftest, so a
residual that is described here is also one that is measured.
`move`, `flow`, `func`, `dot`, `near` and `cadence` are chains, VMs or languages AND they
are ordinary English or Nim words — `move(x)` is a Nim builtin, `func` a Nim keyword. A
ban that a correct reader cannot satisfy gets an exemption written into it, and an
exemption is how a ban stops being one. They are left out, named here, rather than
banned and then excused. `gas` IS banned, because `gas` standing alone as a token in this
reader would be a fee unit and nothing else.
`wasm`, `ink`, `zksync`, `polygon`, `optimism` and `yul` were added after a reviewer
measured them missing. `wasm` is a VM name and this workspace ships three Wasm recorders;
`ink` is Polkadot's language while `polkavm`, its VM, was already banned, so the pair was
half-covered. None of them is an ordinary English or Nim word, so none needs an exemption,
and all six were measured at zero occurrences over every file in scope before landing.

_comment: NO `defaultPath`, DELIBERATELY, and this entry is where the reason belongs.
`ct` was recorded here as the container's default until 2026-09-17 and the
reader never used it — it could not: `transactions[].container` is required
of every traced row and taken by an unguarded subscript, so a traced row that
names no container is REFUSED by S5-ROW-MEMBERS-REQUIRED rather than resolved
to anything. A `defaultPath` here therefore stated a fallback that no code
path can reach, and it had to be hand-exempted from the check that every
default belongs to a container the reader opens — a default that is both
unreachable and excused from the arm that would have said so.
`ct/<txId>.ct` is still the layout every producer in this tree writes, and
§5.1's table still shows it. It is a CONVENTION a producer gets for free,
which §5.1 distinguishes from a default: the row names the file, and if the
row is silent the snapshot is non-conforming.

_nilAccessComment: THE BAN OVER THE FAMILY THAT HAS NOW PRODUCED SEVEN DEFECTS IN THREE MILESTONES:
a member this census marks OPTIONAL, reached by the one access form that cannot
`IndexDefect`, which is not catchable), the position stream's `positioned`/`paths`,
The SCOPE is here rather than in the caller for the reason `chainVocabulary.scope`
is: a scan whose subject lives in a script's habit is a scan whose subject can
shrink without anything going red. It is stated as a ROOT rather than as a file
list, and `snapshot-contract-selftest.mjs` §13 derives the files from the tree under
it — so a new module is in the ban the moment it exists, which a list cannot do.
`shapes` names what is refused and `notCovered` names what is NOT, measured. The
second list is the load-bearing one: this library has already written `banned
outright` about a regex that was not.

shapes.nil-iteration: `for x in node{"k"}` — `items` on the nil node `{}` answers for an absent key dereferences it. `node{"k"}.getElems` answers the empty sequence.
shapes.nil-json-value: `"k": node{"m"}` in a `%*` construction — `%*` stores the nil and `pretty` dereferences it later. `orNull(node{"m"})` is the form.
shapes.nil-dereference: `node{"k"}.len`, `.kind`, `.items`, `[…]` and the rest of `std/json`'s non-nil-tolerant operations, applied directly to a `{}` result. Admissible only when the identical expression is nil-tested first, which Nim's short-circuiting `or` makes safe.

notCovered: `node["k"]` on an optional member — the `KeyError` half of the same family. `[]` is also the correct form for a REQUIRED member, so a token ban on it is unsatisfiable; the reader's half is covered by the census equality check in §2 and nothing else in `src/` is covered at all.
`xs[i]` and `xs[^1]` on a producer-supplied sequence — the `IndexDefect` half. Not a `{}` shape and not scanned.

a `{}` result bound to a name first (`let x = node{"k"}` then `for e in x:`). The widest hole, left open deliberately: closing it needs local dataflow and a rule that guessed would fire on the GUARDED form, which is the repair this ban exists to encourage. Asserted MISSED in §13's attack table.

anything outside `src/` — `client/`, `tools/` and the test suites are not in scope today. Eleven `nil-iteration` sites were measured outside it on 2026-09-17; the five in `client/tests/` were repaired, the six in `tests/` were not.

_comment: §5.4's boundary, stated as NAMES so the claim is checkable rather than a category:
no snapshot-relative path the reader resolves may be one of these.
TWO OF THE SIX HAVE A PRODUCER IN THIS TREE AND FOUR DO NOT, and saying so is the
point rather than an omission. `tools/chain/ingest-range.mjs` writes a
`blocktracer/coverage-ledger@1` at `<state>/coverage.json` and per-range directories
under `<state>/ranges/` — those two are real, and the byte-identity arm in
`tests/tchainsnapshot.nim` plants both beside a real capture. `cursor.json`, `lease`,
`lease.json` and `.lock` are §5.4's OTHER two categories (cursors and leases) with no
instance in this tree today, so the sweep over them is currently vacuous — it would
still catch a reader that learned to open one, which is what the list is for, but a
green over those four is not evidence about anything that exists. `writtenBy` records
which is which so the next reader does not have to grep for it.
_membersComment: AND THE SAME BOUNDARY ONE LEVEL DOWN: a MEMBER a producer here writes into a
snapshot that no reader consumes and §5 therefore does not name. The census above
is the consumed set and is compared to the reader for EQUALITY in both directions,
so such a member cannot live in it — and until 2026-09-17 that meant it lived
nowhere at all, which is how `counts.captureSessions` came to be required of every
committed snapshot by a self-test while being absent from this file entirely. A
hand-authored snapshot written from §5 alone then failed a rule §5 does not state.
So they are recorded here, OPTIONAL by construction: a conforming producer may omit
every one of them, and the only thing asserted about them is that ours writes them.
`writtenBy` follows the same convention as the path list above — the file that
writes it, or `null` for a member this tree has no producer for — and
`snapshot-contract-selftest.mjs` §12 holds three things about each: that it is NOT
in the consumed census, that the named writer really writes it, and that the reader
does not read it. A member that became consumed would fail all three rather than
sitting here as a stale note.
THE LIST WAS ONE MEMBER LONG UNTIL 2026-09-17 AND `recount.mjs` WRITES THIRTEEN.
`captureSessions` was recorded because a self-test had made it load-bearing; the other
twelve were in exactly the same position — written by our producer, opened by no
reader, named by no section — and their only distinction was that nothing had tripped
over them yet. Two of them had already been WRONGLY promoted by §5.2's prose, which
called `counts.privateOnly` and the per-reason `counts.refusals` block required while
the census named neither and neither conformance-kit template carried them: a
hand-authored tree written from §5 alone was conforming and non-conforming at once,
depending on which half of the document you read. Recording the whole set is what
stops the next one being discovered the same way.

memberHolds.snapshot.counts.captureSessions: how many supervised watch sessions contributed to this capture, or `null` when the `captures` member is not countable. Optional: §5 names no such member, no reader opens it, and a snapshot without it is conforming. `tools/chain/refusal-selftest.mjs` requires it of THIS repository's captures and of nothing else.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.blocksWithTransactions: how many of the enumerated blocks settled at least one transaction. Optional: no reader opens it, and a snapshot without it is conforming.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.bodyRetained: how many rows recorded the node still serving their body at capture. Optional: no reader opens it, and a snapshot without it is conforming.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.replayed: how many rows carry the `replayed` outcome. Optional: no reader opens it, and a snapshot without it is conforming.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.divergent: how many rows carry the `divergent` outcome. Optional: no reader opens it, and a snapshot without it is conforming.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.refused: how many rows carry the `refused` outcome. Optional: no reader opens it, and a snapshot without it is conforming.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.pruned: how many rows carry the `pruned` outcome. Optional: no reader opens it, and a snapshot without it is conforming.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.tracesPublished: `replayed` plus `divergent` — the traced population's size. Optional: no reader opens it, and a snapshot without it is conforming.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.refusals: the per-reason tally of untraced rows, keyed by `refusalReason`. §5.2's prose called this required until 2026-09-17; the census never named it, no reader opens it, and neither conformance-kit template carries it. Optional, like every member here.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.refusalsTotal: how many untraced rows carry a classified `refusalReason`. Optional: no reader opens it, and a snapshot without it is conforming.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.refusalsUnclassified: how many untraced rows carry none. Optional: no reader opens it, and a snapshot without it is conforming.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.privateOnly: how many rows are chain-absent. §5.2's prose called this required until 2026-09-17, on the same mistake `refusals` was made by, and for the same reason it is optional: the census never named it and no reader opens it.
memberHolds.snapshot.counts.untraced: the untraced population's size. Optional: no reader opens it, and a snapshot without it is conforming.
